structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E015.
1. Accuracy has come from three places: averaging (E005, about +1.0 pp), Muon (E006, +0.66 pp) and pixels or capacity in the final phase (E007 resizing was about neutral; the 20 px schedule in E011 cost 1.4 pp; the 512 width in E010 cost 0.43 pp, paid back with +0.5 epoch to reach 9.5). Scalar knobs on top of Muon+Lookahead are flat. In E013, LS 0.3→0.2 gave +0.04 pp. In E014, Muon lr ×1.5 gave +0.10 pp. In E009, LR→0 gave -0.26 pp. All three are inside the reshuffle noise.
2. New evidence on noise: E015 claims identical math (CUDA graphs), yet its accuracy moved from 0.7548 to 0.7574 (+0.27 pp). Any kernel or fusion change reshuffles the per-seed trajectories by about ±0.3 pp on the 3-seed mean, even when the math is "identical". A re-run of the same binary is bit-identical (E012), so the tip's 0.7574 is partly a lucky draw. Its true expected value is closer to about 0.756. The loop risks selecting on noise: each keep picks the lucky reshuffle. The 40-seed mean is the real risk, and the E012 held-out result is still unreported.
3. Weight decay is nearly inert. Muon applies no WD, and the filters are renormalized to fixed norm every step. WD touches only the BN biases, the whitening bias and the head. Halving it is a reshuffle.
4. My proposed mechanism, which nobody else has named, is Lookahead on Muon's fixed-norm sphere. Averaging unit-norm filters shrinks their norm, and Muon's next step renormalizes them. Each pull therefore acts as an angular damper plus a reset to a consensus point. Because BN follows every conv, the function is unchanged, but the effective step size is altered. A plain write-only EMA (I022) loses this. Given the cubic alpha ramp, it is also effectively just a roughly 20-step late average, and its averaged BN stats are mismatched. Expect -0.3 to -0.8 pp.
5. Time is GPU compute. CUDA graphs bought under 1% (6.64→6.58 s), which confirms that launch overhead is small. What remains on the host side is the per-epoch work: a 25-mask boolean crop loop (it syncs), the antialias interpolate, and the 50k gather. That is maybe 1-3%. The real time levers are FLOPs, meaning resolution allocation, epochs and width. The 32 px phase (30% of steps at full cost) dominates. Moving the 28→32 switch later, or adding a short 32 px tail, could save about 5% if accuracy is set mainly in the final phase. That is the cheapest untested lever.
6. Time noise is about ±1%.
Unsure: the 40-seed and held-out mean of the tip; whether Muon's lr_t fill and the Lookahead foreach ops force graph re-records; the cost of prepare (about 0.2 s).

forecasts.reason: Muon filters get no WD; halving only touches BN/head biases, so the result is a reshuffle, not a +0.3 pp gain over the current setting.
The step is already graphed; only the per-epoch augment syncs and the LR scalar writes remain, so expect about 1-3% saved, borderline for the 3% threshold; fusion reshuffles accuracy.
The Lookahead write-back damps Muon's fixed-norm trajectory; a write-only EMA with the cubic ramp only averages the last ~20 steps and mismatches the BN stats.

cruxes: What did E012's held-out seeds 3-12 give for the tip-like recipe? If the mean sits more than 0.2 pp below seeds 0-2, the tip (0.7574, partly a lucky kernel reshuffle) is fragile for the 40-seed judgment, and epochs must go up, not down.

Is accuracy set mainly in the final 32 px phase? Shrinking the 32 px share (for example, 24 px for 50%, 28 px for 30%, 32 px for 20%) at fixed epochs would test whether about 5% of FLOPs can be removed without an accuracy loss.

Does the Lookahead write-back matter because of Muon's fixed-norm sphere (I022 loses ≥0.3 pp) or because of endpoint averaging (I022 within 0.3 pp)? The answer decides whether averaging variants are worth exploring.
